headline: Gulf crude flows at ~80% of prewar
dek: Brent traded near $110 (tested $110.70 Oct 17-19, highest since May 20), WTI near $99; Brent +80% in 2026. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright (Fox News): Gulf crude flows recovered to ~80% of prewar, refined products still constrained.
sources: Dow Jones Market Talk via TradingView; Bloomberg via Moneyweb; Reuters via substack readout
fault_line: Pocketbook angle: who pays for Hormuz? Households facing +80% Brent in a year vs governments insisting 'flows are recovering.' Is $110 the new normal, or will the escort/blockade equilibrium crack?

sections.what_happened: Brent traded near $110 (tested $110.70 Oct 17-19, highest since May 20), WTI near $99; Brent +80% in 2026. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright (Fox News): Gulf crude flows recovered to ~80% of prewar, refined products still constrained. Iran First VP Mohammad Reza Aref (IRNA, Oct 19, meeting Russian PM Mishustin in Tajikistan): Iran has 'no other choice' but to assert control over Hormuz for its security; Iran could ensure safe passage for friendly countries.
sections.what_verified: Multiple market desks (Bloomberg/Moneyweb, Dow Jones/TradingView, Business Times, Free Press Journal). Aref remarks via IRNA corroborated across Bloomberg/IANS copies.
sections.what_disputed: Substack analyst cautions Saudi authorities had not confirmed some reported Ansar Allah attacks on Saudi facilities cited in the Reuters readout — treat those specific claims as unverified.
sections.why_matters: Lead with the household: Brent up 80% this year, your petrol bill is the war's receipt. Two parallel truths — markets say 'five-month high,' Washington says '80% recovered.' Pocketbook-first explainer with map of the strait and the mine/escort duel.
